question: Which nursing documentation detail is essential after finishing a gastric lavage session?

options.A: The brand name and factory serial number of the lavage tube
options.B: Total amounts of fluid put in and taken out of the stomach
options.C: The exact weight of the patient measured in kilograms
options.D: The name of the family member who gave consent for care

explanation: Recording fluid balance prevents water intoxication or electrolyte imbalances, confirming that the nurse recovered roughly what was instilled. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: A patient treated for a wasp sting allergy feels fine after 30 minutes and wants to go home. What should you tell them?

options.A: Explain that the patient must stay longer because a secondary reaction can happen hours later
options.B: Tell the patient that once symptoms stop, they will never have another reaction
options.C: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to be completely safe before leaving
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines

explanation: Allergic reactions can strike twice! We call this a biphasic reaction, meaning the patient needs to stick around for observation just in case symptoms return hours later.

question: What famous global health goal was established at the 1978 Alma-Ata conference?

options.A: Eradication of Malaria by 1985
options.B: Universal Hospital Access by 1990
options.C: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.D: Free Tertiary Care for Every Citizen

explanation: The Alma-Ata conference set the ambitious global target of achieving 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: A staff nurse wants to move from a general ward into the busy Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Which benefit of continuing education makes this possible?

options.A: Reducing hospital expenses
options.B: Lowering patient admission rates
options.C: Promoting specialization
options.D: Simplifying medical records

explanation: Specialization gives you the exact skills and confidence you need to step into advanced areas like the ICU or theatre. You can grow your career step by step!

question: In clinical nursing, what is a 'toxidrome'?

options.A: An antidote given to reverse the effects of a specific snake venom
options.B: A group of signs and symptoms pointing to a specific class of poison
options.C: The physical damage caused by corrosive chemicals on the skin
options.D: The laboratory test used to measure blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Think of a toxidrome as a symptom 'syndrome' caused by a 'toxic' substance. It helps nurses quickly spot what kind of poison is at play!

question: What is the gold-standard test to confirm a patient truly has gout?

options.A: Performing a standard chest X-ray on the patient
options.B: Measuring the daily protein intake in the diet
options.C: Checking a routine blood pressure reading in the clinic
options.D: Examining joint fluid under a microscope for crystals

explanation: You got it! Drawing a little fluid out of the angry joint and spotting those sneaky uric acid crystals under a microscope gives a 100% definite diagnosis.

question: What is the biggest threat to keeping a primary nursing unit running smoothly?

options.A: Patients refusing to learn their primary nurse's first name
options.B: Physicians refusing to write orders for patients assigned to primary nurses
options.C: An excess of medical equipment in the hospital storage rooms
options.D: A shortage of qualified registered nurses leading to unmanageable workloads

explanation: When nurse numbers drop too low, it becomes impossible for one nurse to give deep, continuous care to multiple patients at once.

question: You are caring for a patient with long-standing diabetes. Which assessment is key for tertiary prevention of microvascular issues?

options.A: Measuring handgrip strength using a dynamometer
options.B: Palpating superficial lymph nodes in the neck
options.C: Asking about daily recreational screen time habits
options.D: Checking urine for microalbumin and performing foot exams

explanation: Spot on! Checking urine for tiny amounts of protein (microalbumin) and inspecting the feet regularly helps catch early kidney and nerve damage.

question: Why does an inflamed cervix tend to bleed easily during an examination?

options.A: Complete destruction of the underlying muscle layer
options.B: Fragile tissues and tiny blood vessels opening up from inflammation
options.C: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells by the cervix
options.D: Severe blood clotting disorders throughout the body

explanation: When tissue is inflamed, blood rushes to the area and the vessels become delicate, meaning even a gentle touch can cause spotting.

question: If a patient has a growth causing uncontrolled hypersecretion of a hormone, what happens?

options.A: Complete shutdown of all nervous system reflex pathways
options.B: An exaggerated physiological response and metabolic disturbance
options.C: Permanent cessation of all tropic hormone production
options.D: Immediate reversal of normal circadian rhythm patterns

explanation: 'Hyper-' means too much! Overproducing hormones puts target organs into overdrive, causing clear signs of imbalance.

question: What is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Severe dietary calcium deficiency
options.B: Chronic inflammation of the thyroid
options.C: Autoimmune destruction of the glands
options.D: A benign parathyroid adenoma

explanation: Most of the time, primary hyperparathyroidism is caused by a single non-cancerous (benign) growth or adenoma on one of the parathyroid glands.

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when a worker gets a deep cut at work?

options.A: Ask the worker to fill out an insurance claim form first
options.B: Provide immediate first aid and stabilize the worker
options.C: Wait for the company director to arrive and give permission
options.D: Send the worker home without examining the wound

explanation: Always remember your nursing ABCs and emergency priorities—patient safety and immediate first aid come before any paperwork!

question: Which of these is a typical feature of a benign (non-cancerous) tumor?

options.A: Surrounded by a fibrous capsule
options.B: Infiltrates surrounding normal tissues
options.C: Rapid and uncontrolled cellular division
options.D: Ability to form secondary tumors

explanation: Correct! Benign tumors usually stay put inside a neat fibrous capsule, meaning they don't invade nearby tissues or spread around.

question: How does lowering dietary protein help a patient with severe liver failure?

options.A: It prevents a dangerous buildup of toxic ammonia in the blood
options.B: It lowers the patient's blood pressure back to normal
options.C: It allows the liver to regenerate new cells overnight
options.D: It stops internal bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: A failing liver cannot process ammonia properly, so reducing dietary protein lowers the amount of ammonia produced in the gut. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h2)

question: What does variability tell us about a set of patient data?

options.A: The exact middle value of a data set
options.B: The total sum of all recorded patient observations
options.C: The spread or scatter of data points around a central value
options.D: The most frequently occurring measurement in a study

explanation: Great job thinking about data! Variability simply shows how bunched up or spread out patient numbers are from the average.

question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks ANC gets mosquito nets and iron supplements. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic sex of the baby
options.B: To induce early labor in high-risk situations
options.C: To prevent malaria and treat or prevent anemia
options.D: To stop morning sickness during the first trimester

explanation: Malaria and low blood (anemia) are major risks in pregnancy, so nets and iron are standard lifesavers in our clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: Which common anti-TB drug is famous for turning urine and tears a harmless red-orange color?

options.A: Ethambutol
options.B: Isoniazid
options.C: Pyrazinamide
options.D: Rifampicin

explanation: Rifampicin gives body fluids a reddish tint. As a nurse, warning your patients about this beforehand saves them a lot of panic!

question: How does long-term high blood pressure change the structure of the heart muscle over time?

options.A: It cures high blood pressure by strengthening the valves
options.B: It repairs damaged arteries and restores normal blood flow
options.C: It changes the shape and thickness of the heart muscle, leading to weak pumping
options.D: It shrinks the heart chambers back to normal sizes

explanation: Just like lifting heavy weights builds your biceps, fighting high pressure makes the heart walls thicken and change shape, which eventually wears it out.

question: Why should you avoid using heavy medical slang when talking to a new patient?

options.A: It shows the nurse is not confident in clinical procedures
options.B: It wastes valuable time during the admission assessment process
options.C: It breaks hospital documentation rules and charting standards
options.D: It can confuse the patient and lead to misunderstandings about care

explanation: Using simple, everyday language ensures the patient truly understands what is happening with their health.

question: A patient with severe liver disease is prescribed a medication that is normally broken down by hepatic enzymes. What is the most appropriate nursing concern?

options.A: The liver disease will instantly cure itself once the pill is swallowed
options.B: The drug may build up in the body and cause toxic effects
options.C: The medication will pass through the body without any effect at all
options.D: The drug will be eliminated too quickly to provide any relief

explanation: A damaged liver cannot metabolize drugs effectively, leading to dangerous levels accumulating in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h4)

question: What does the term polyuria mean in a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Severe pain and burning sensation during urination
options.B: Excessive production and passing of urine
options.C: A sudden and total inability to pass any urine
options.D: An intense, constant craving for sweet foods

explanation: Polyuria refers to passing large volumes of urine, which happens when excess sugar pulls extra water out of the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: In a healthy human body, where do normal prion proteins naturally live?

options.A: Along the lining of the gut
options.B: On the membranes of neurons
options.C: Inside red blood cells
options.D: Within the fluid of joints

explanation: You got it! Normal prions hang out peacefully on the surface membranes of our nerve cells. It's only when they change shape that trouble starts.

question: Why might a nurse relax a patient's long-standing diabetic diet restrictions during palliative care?

options.A: Sugar has no effect on blood glucose in terminal patients
options.B: Strict dietary control is no longer relevant to their comfort and quality of life
options.C: Diabetes automatically cures itself in advanced illness
options.D: Patients with terminal illnesses can no longer taste sweetness

explanation: You nailed it! Chronic disease rules are meant for long-term health. In palliative care, bringing a smile with a sweet treat matters much more.

question: A home care nurse visits an elderly patient who just had a hip replacement. What is the most important safety tip to give them?

options.A: Remove loose throw rugs from all walkways
options.B: Keep all windows open wide for fresh air circulation
options.C: Paint all indoor stairs a bright neon color
options.D: Turn off all lights at night to save electrical energy

explanation: Loose rugs are a major trap for feet and frequently cause falls. Clearing the floor keeps your patient safe at home!

question: Why is it important for a primary health care nurse in a rural Nigerian community to understand seasonal disease patterns?

options.A: To accurately predict the winner of upcoming local political elections
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of imported medical equipment
options.C: To schedule annual leave during the busiest months of the year
options.D: To anticipate outbreaks like meningitis or cholera and prepare preventive supplies early

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing when seasonal illnesses like meningitis or cholera peak helps clinics stock up and protect the community on time. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when breaking the news of a death to family members?

options.A: It forces the family to ask the physician for translation
options.B: It is against hospital accreditation rules to use medical terms
options.C: It can cause confusion and prevent them from grasping the reality of the loss
options.D: It makes the nurse sound unprofessional and uneducated

explanation: Spot on! Using plain, simple language ensures grieving relatives truly understand what happened without getting confused by big words.

question: A student with asthma starts wheezing badly during sports. What should the school nurse do first?

options.A: Send the student home immediately without any medical assessment
options.B: Tell the student to run faster to clear their airways naturally
options.C: Assess the student and administer the prescribed rescue inhaler
options.D: Wait until the end of the school day to notify the parents

explanation: You got it! The nurse needs to quickly check the student and give their emergency rescue inhaler as outlined in their care plan.

question: What is the main goal when medical help arrives immediately after a disaster?

options.A: To minimize death and illness
options.B: To train local volunteers
options.C: To rebuild damaged hospitals
options.D: To document insurance claims

explanation: You've got this! When disaster strikes, the immediate focus is always on saving lives and stopping severe illness through quick medical action.

question: Why does a patient not feel pain when a surgeon touches the actual brain tissue during a procedure?

options.A: Anesthesia freezes all nerves permanently
options.B: The brain tissue lacks pain receptors
options.C: The skull blocks pain signals from escaping
options.D: The dura mater numbs the rest of the brain

explanation: Because brain tissue has no nociceptors, pain is only felt when surrounding structures like the scalp, blood vessels, or meninges are irritated. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is an important nursing duty when giving a wearable device to a patient?

options.A: Writing custom software code to link the device to the hospital
options.B: Calibrating the internal microchips using a sterile surgical kit
options.C: Teaching the patient how to wear, charge, and sync the device
options.D: Replacing the device hardware components whenever the battery dies

explanation: As a nurse, your guidance is key! Patients need to know how to handle, charge, and sync their devices so the data keeps flowing.

question: What is the main risk of breastfeeding when a mother is living with HIV?

options.A: Severe malnutrition in the nursing infant
options.B: Transmission of the virus through breast milk
options.C: Rapid maternal immune system collapse
options.D: Permanent loss of breast milk production

explanation: You've got this! While breast milk is packed with goodness, it can unfortunately pass the virus from an infected mum to her baby during feeding. Understanding this helps us support mums better!

question: When giving a bed bath, in what direction should you wash the skin?

options.A: From the feet up to the face
options.B: From dirtiest areas to cleanest areas
options.C: From the left side to the right side
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtier areas

explanation: Brilliant! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag germs from lower areas up onto sensitive spots like the face.

question: How do patients dealing with heavy stress often present themselves in the clinic?

options.A: With sudden weight gain and lower blood pressure
options.B: With visible joy and high energy levels
options.C: With physical complaints like headaches, insomnia, and body pains
options.D: With enhanced memory and sharp focus

explanation: Emotional stress loves to hide in physical symptoms. When patients can't sleep or have endless body aches, stress is often the culprit!

question: What makes a portal system different from normal blood circulation?

options.A: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs to the brain
options.B: It pumps blood directly from veins into arteries without using capillaries
options.C: It connects two capillary beds through a vein before returning to the heart
options.D: It bypasses the heart completely using specialized lymphatic vessels

explanation: Think of a portal system as a special detour! Instead of going straight back to the heart, blood flows through one capillary bed, travels through a vein, and hits a second capillary bed first. You're doing great!

question: How do hard structures like bones usually look on a standard ultrasound image?

options.A: As glowing green areas showing high activity
options.B: They block the sound and leave a dark shadow behind them
options.C: As completely clear, empty spaces
options.D: As bright white lines that let sound pass right through

explanation: Bone bounces most of the sound back, preventing the waves from going deeper—this creates what we call an acoustic shadow behind it.

question: Why do night-shift nurses often find it hard to sleep during the day? Daytime light affects which hormone?

options.A: Aldosterone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Daylight tells your biological clock to keep melatonin levels low, which is why sleeping during the day after a night shift can be so tough.

question: Why do red blood cells end up leaking into the urine when someone has Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Severe infection inside the urinary meatus
options.B: Rapid breakdown of muscular tissue in the legs
options.C: Direct physical trauma to the external bladder lining
options.D: The damaged filtering membrane becomes too porous

explanation: When inflammation damages the filter, the tiny holes become too wide (porous)—letting red blood cells slip right through into the urine. Makes sense, right?

question: What is the main goal of giving antiplatelet drugs like aspirin for circulation problems?

options.A: To prevent blood platelets from clumping together and forming clots
options.B: To lower systemic blood pressure by reducing total blood volume
options.C: To dissolve existing large blood clots rapidly in emergency settings
options.D: To widen narrowed blood vessels by relaxing their smooth muscle

explanation: Aspirin and friends act like peacekeepers for your platelets, stopping them from sticking together into stubborn roadblocks inside your blood vessels.

question: What is a major danger when public clinics run out of basic medicines (stockouts)?

options.A: Hospitals automatically receive double their budget allocation
options.B: Doctors start prescribing fewer medications to save money
options.C: Pharmaceutical companies lower their international prices
options.D: Patients lose trust and may buy unsafe drugs from roadside vendors

explanation: Exactly. When shelves are empty, desperate patients turn to the street, exposing themselves to dangerous counterfeit drugs.

question: How do adsorbent drugs help ease diarrhoea symptoms?

options.A: They bind to toxins and fluid on their surface
options.B: They increase blood flow to the intestinal lining
options.C: They paralyze the nerves of the large intestine
options.D: They stimulate the production of healthy gut bacteria

explanation: Think of adsorbents like a sponge in the gut—they grab onto bad toxins and extra liquid, carrying them safely out in the stool.

question: Which adaptive tool helps a patient with shaky hands eat on their own?

options.A: A long-handled reacher
options.B: Weighted utensils
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A rigid gait belt

explanation: You got it! Heavy spoons and forks help steady shaky hands so food actually makes it to the mouth.

question: Which common food is sometimes restricted for young children due to the old myth that it makes them steal?

options.A: Eggs
options.B: Yam
options.C: Beans
options.D: Rice

explanation: An old local myth falsely claims that feeding eggs to young children makes them prone to stealing. In reality, eggs are fantastic protein sources for growing kids!

question: Which part of the nervous system handles the emission phase of ejaculation?

options.A: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.B: Enteric nervous system
options.C: Central nervous system only
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your 'fight, flight, and function' gear! It sends the signals that move semen forward into the urethra.

question: An elderly patient is finding it hard to press a metered-dose inhaler and breathe in slowly at the same time. What is a great alternative device?

options.A: An unassisted MDI
options.B: A dry powder inhaler
options.C: A compressor nebulizer
options.D: A nasal cannula

explanation: Nebulizers are wonderful for patients who struggle with coordination because they turn liquid medicine into a continuous mist, allowing the patient to just breathe normally.

question: A patient is given a minor tranquilizer for short-term stress. What key safety advice should you give them before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how the drug affects you
options.B: Mix the medication with a glass of wine to help it absorb faster
options.C: Stop taking the pills abruptly whenever you feel better
options.D: Double the dose if your stress level doubles during the day

explanation: Because these drugs cause drowsiness and slow down reflexes, patients need to steer clear of hazardous tasks until they see how their body reacts.

question: How do many patients in Nigerian communities often describe emotional distress?

options.A: Through physical sensations like body heat or crawling feelings in the head
options.B: By refusing to speak to any family members
options.C: Through formal psychological diagnostic terminology
options.D: By requesting immediate admission to specialized trauma wards

explanation: In many cultures, emotional pain shows up physically in the body—like feeling hot all over or crawling sensations in the head. Good nurses know to listen for these clues!

question: What is the main benefit of involving local residents in data collection?

options.A: It allows nurses to stay inside the office all day long
options.B: It builds local ownership and trust in health programs
options.C: It forces community members to pay taxes to the clinic
options.D: It removes the need for professional nursing training

explanation: When residents participate in the diagnostic process, they value the resulting health interventions and support them willingly. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why are DMARDs prescribed for clients with inflammatory joint diseases?

options.A: To provide instant pain relief during a severe acute flare
options.B: To rebuild lost cartilage within the damaged joint space
options.C: To slow down disease progression and joint damage
options.D: To permanently cure the underlying autoimmune response

explanation: DMARDs (Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs) don't just mask pain; they step in to slow down the immune attack and protect the joints from long-term destruction.

question: What type of power does a nurse have simply because they were officially appointed as the shift charge nurse?

options.A: Referent power
options.B: Coercive power
options.C: Expert power
options.D: Legitimate power

explanation: Correct! Legitimate power comes directly from your official job title or position in the hospital hierarchy.

question: Which part of the body naturally produces cortisol?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Adrenal cortex
options.C: Pancreatic islets
options.D: Posterior pituitary

explanation: Cortisol is a natural stress hormone made and released by the outer layer of your adrenal glands, called the adrenal cortex. You've got this!

question: Why is healthcare different from buying regular goods at the market?

options.A: Illness is unpredictable and human survival is at stake
options.B: Hospitals never face constraints on equipment or staffing
options.C: Medical services are always provided free of charge by the state
options.D: Patients always know exactly what medical treatment they require

explanation: Spot on! You can plan when to buy shoes, but sickness catches you off guard. Because lives are on the line, healthcare doesn't follow normal business rules.

question: Why should you check back in after a conflict has supposedly been settled?

options.A: To punish anyone who failed to follow the new rules
options.B: To write a formal disciplinary report for the human resources file
options.C: To verify that the agreed solution is actually working in practice
options.D: To ensure the conflict is brought up again at the next meeting

explanation: Agreements look great on paper, but a quick follow-up ensures people are actually following through during busy shifts.

question: Why is it super important to keep the scale on your vertical axis even and consistent?

options.A: To ensure the graph fits inside a standard notebook page margin
options.B: To prevent the visual representation from distorting the reality of the data
options.C: To make all data points land on the exact same numerical value
options.D: To eliminate the need for drawing connecting line segments

explanation: Great job! If your spacing is uneven, small changes can look like huge emergencies, which can easily mislead readers.

question: What term describes the wear and tear on the body from long-term, ongoing stress?

options.A: Systemic exhaustion
options.B: Adverse adaptation
options.C: Allostatic load
options.D: Homeostatic balance

explanation: 'Allostatic load' is just a fancy way of saying your body gets tired and worn down from fighting stress day after day without a break.

question: Which past surgery is most likely to cause scar tissue (adhesions) that could affect future fertility?

options.A: Pelvic surgery or surgery inside the lower belly
options.B: Appendectomy on the arm
options.C: Tonsillectomy
options.D: Knee arthroscopy

explanation: Surgeries close to the reproductive organs can leave behind small bands of scar tissue that might twist or block the fallopian tubes. Good to keep in mind!

question: Why must a nurse keep a strict 'chain of custody' when handling forensic evidence?

options.A: To ensure the collected evidence is legally admissible in court
options.B: To reduce hospital supply and inventory costs
options.C: To diagnose underlying sexually transmitted infections faster
options.D: To speed up the patient's physical recovery process

explanation: Keeping strict track of who handles evidence stops it from getting lost or tampered with so it can actually help get justice in court.

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain.

question: What is the primary danger of delaying stock card updates until the end of the week?

options.A: Hospital management will reduce the overall budget of the nursing unit
options.B: The central store will automatically double the next order quantity
options.C: Arithmetic errors and forgotten items lead to inaccurate stock balances
options.D: The medications on the shelf will automatically change their expiry dates

explanation: Relying on memory hours or days later results in guessing quantities, which destroys the reliability of the inventory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why is checking daily on chronic illnesses so important in a home setting?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests entirely
options.B: It proves to the insurance company that nursing visits are unnecessary
options.C: It completely cures chronic conditions without the need for medications
options.D: It helps catch early warning signs before a hospital admission is needed

explanation: Exactly right! Catching small changes early lets you and the medical team step in quickly, keeping the patient out of the hospital ward. Excellent clinical intuition!

question: A patient taking a daily anticoagulant medication reports finding dark, tarry stools. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A normal reaction to eating green leafy vegetables
options.B: Rapid dehydration due to warm weather conditions
options.C: Bleeding somewhere in the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: An infection caused by low white blood cell counts

explanation: Dark, tarry stools indicate digested blood coming from the stomach or upper gut, which is a sign of bleeding caused by anticoagulants. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why does batch cooking help save money?

options.A: It guarantees that food will never spoil under any condition
options.B: It requires buying expensive kitchen appliances upfront
options.C: It forces family members to eat less food overall
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and limits ingredient waste

explanation: Spot on! Cooking larger pots at once uses less cooking gas or kerosene and ensures ingredients get used up before going bad.

question: Why should you always leave a little 'buffer time' in your daily shift plan?

options.A: To account for unpredictable emergencies and interruptions
options.B: To guarantee a full hour for lunch without a handover
options.C: To ensure doctors finish their rounds on time
options.D: To reduce the number of required patient assessments

explanation: Hospitals are super unpredictable! Leaving a little unassigned wiggle room in your schedule helps you handle sudden surprises without throwing off your whole day.

question: In elderly care, why do nurses look at a patient's physical ability rather than just their birth certificate?

options.A: Because chronological age alone does not reflect physical strength or health status
options.B: Because chronological age can be altered easily with basic exercises
options.C: Because hospital funding depends entirely on a patient's exact birth year
options.D: Because physiological age remains identical in every person over sixty

explanation: Spot on! Two people of the exact same age can have very different physical fitness levels depending on their lifelong habits and health.

question: Why is keeping a steady level of calcium in your body so important for daily function?

options.A: It prevents the pancreas from producing too much digestive acid.
options.B: It is required for proper nerve conduction and muscle contraction.
options.C: It maintains the normal filtering pressure inside the liver lobules.
options.D: It directly controls the total volume of circulating red blood cells.

explanation: Calcium is essential for sending nerve signals and making your muscles move smoothly. Without it, your nerves and muscles simply cannot function right!

question: What is the standard formula used to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared
options.B: Height in meters divided by weight in pounds squared
options.C: Weight in pounds multiplied by height in inches
options.D: Height in centimeters divided by weight in kilograms

explanation: You got it! Weight in kg divided by height in meters squared ($kg/m^2$) is the classic formula you will use all through your nursing practice.

question: What is a potential long-term complication for an infant who survives a severe intracranial hemorrhage?

options.A: Developmental delays and seizure disorders
options.B: Early closure of all body joints
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of smell only
options.D: Enlargement of the hands and feet

explanation: Significant bleeding inside the cranium can damage brain tissue, leading to chronic neurological issues like seizures and delayed milestones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h6)

question: How long should you ask clients to wait at the clinic after getting a vaccine?

options.A: 15 to 30 minutes
options.B: Until the end of the day
options.C: No waiting time is necessary
options.D: Exactly 2 hours

explanation: Severe allergic reactions usually happen shortly after an injection. Keeping patients for a few minutes lets us monitor and help them immediately if needed.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle vaccine hesitancy from a caregiver?

options.A: Telling the caregiver that their personal beliefs are completely wrong
options.B: Listening respectfully to concerns and providing clear facts
options.C: Threatening to withhold other basic primary healthcare services
options.D: Ignoring the questions and quickly administering the injection anyway

explanation: You nailed it! Building trust through patience, empathy, and gentle education works way better than arguing or judging.

question: Where in the human body would you exclusively find suture joints?

options.A: In the skull
options.B: In the spine
options.C: In the pelvis
options.D: In the fingers

explanation: Exactly! Sutures are those tight, fibrous interlocking lines holding the flat bones of your skull together securely.

question: A client presents with a sudden worsening cough and shortness of breath. Which interview question is most important to ask first?

options.A: How many family members have asthma?
options.B: What kind of work did you do thirty years ago?
options.C: Are you allergic to any specific types of food?
options.D: When did these breathing symptoms actually start?

explanation: Determining the onset and timeline of acute symptoms is the immediate priority during a symptom analysis for a sudden respiratory change. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h2)

question: What makes epilepsy different from having just one isolated seizure?

options.A: Epilepsy involves recurrent, unprovoked seizures over time
options.B: Epilepsy can only be diagnosed using a blood test
options.C: Epilepsy only occurs in children under the age of five

question: Why does joint looseness during pregnancy make women more prone to muscle or joint injury?

question: What is the main job of the thalamus in the brain?

question: Who are the typical core members of a multidisciplinary rehabilitation team?

question: Why should a home health nurse try to interview an older patient alone during a home visit?

question: Why are administrative decisions much better when they are backed by nursing research?

question: Why is involving family members in dietary education so important for these patients?

question: Why must a patient take off their daily nitroglycerin skin patch for a few hours every day?

question: What main substance does a Nelson inhaler deliver to help a patient breathe better?

question: What is the main goal of planning a personal diet for a patient?

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?

question: Why must public health nurses examine social and economic factors in a community?

options.C: Global Import Tariff Book

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention strategies regarding gender-based violence?

options.A: Prosecuting offenders swiftly in a court of law
options.B: Stopping violence before it ever occurs by changing social norms
options.C: Treating physical injuries in the emergency room after an attack
options.D: Providing long-term counseling years after an assault

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping the root causes of violence before any abusive incident takes place. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h4)

question: What happens to blood vessels when they are exposed to a lot of heat?

options.A: Vasoconstriction, which completely stops blood circulation
options.B: Thrombosis of all major pelvic arteries
options.C: Vasodilation, which increases blood flow to the area
options.D: Immediate sclerosis and permanent vessel collapse

explanation: You've got this! Heat causes blood vessels to relax and widen (vasodilation), which brings more blood flow right to that warmed area.

question: What is a recommended eating pattern to help reduce nausea during early pregnancy?

options.A: Eating small, frequent meals throughout the day
options.B: Eating three large meals loaded with healthy fats
options.C: Fasting until the afternoon to let the stomach rest
options.D: Drinking a large glass of water right before every meal

explanation: Keeping a little food in the stomach prevents the empty-stomach feeling that often worsens nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: Why can using harsh, strong soaps every day damage the skin?

options.A: They permanently block all normal sweat gland secretions
options.B: They strip away the natural protective lipid barrier
options.C: They increase the thickness of the subcutaneous fat layer
options.D: They cause an immediate and permanent loss of skin pigment

explanation: Exactly! Harsh soaps wash away your skin's friendly natural oils, leaving it dry, angry, and irritated.

question: How does high blood pressure cause damage to a patient's kidneys?

options.A: High pressure strains and hardens the delicate blood vessels in the glomeruli
options.B: Hypertension directly causes the bladder to shrink
options.C: High blood pressure washes away all the red blood cells in the body
options.D: High pressure stops the heart from pumping blood to the lungs

explanation: Think of high pressure like a rushing river beating against a weak fence. It puts harsh mechanical stress on tiny kidney capillaries, causing them to scar over time.

question: Why is keeping a proper inventory of family planning supplies so important at a clinic?

options.A: It ensures expired drugs get handed out very fast
options.B: It means you don't have to write daily attendance records
options.C: It lets the nurse sell extra supplies for side cash
options.D: It stops stock-outs so clients don't suddenly run out of their method

explanation: Great thinking! Running out of supplies leaves patients stranded and unprotected, so tracking inventory keeps care running smoothly.

question: How does nursing in the community differ from working in a big hospital ward?

options.A: Home nurses rely heavily on resourcefulness and critical thinking in the community.
options.B: Home nurses have direct access to immediate physician support at all times.
options.C: Hospital nurses perform fewer physical assessments than community nurses.
options.D: Hospital nurses manage fewer complex chronic conditions than home nurses.

explanation: You got it! Without hospital equipment and doctors right next door, home care nurses have to trust their training, think on their feet, and solve problems creatively.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.C: Maternal education and literacy rates
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why do we study occupational health risks in nursing?

options.A: To help nurses stay safe and maintain a healthy career
options.B: To reduce the financial expenses of the hospital management
options.C: To eliminate all physical tasks from daily nursing duties
options.D: To ensure patients recover faster from their illnesses

explanation: Spotting workplace hazards early helps you protect your own health so you can enjoy a long, injury-free nursing journey. You matter too!

question: Why is it better to call for an emergency medical assistance team early instead of waiting for a full cardiac arrest?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.
options.B: It keeps the hospital hallways quiet during visiting hours.
options.C: It prevents doctors from having to do paperwork later.
options.D: It allows the team to treat the underlying cause before the heart stops.

explanation: Once a patient's heart stops, their chance of surviving intact drops significantly compared to catching and fixing the problem while they still have a pulse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h6)

question: A nurse is sent to a remote village with no motorable roads or clinic. What kind of situation is this?

options.A: Single parents with plenty of cash
options.B: Internally displaced persons waiting for homes
options.C: Rural families facing geographic and infrastructure challenges
options.D: Urban rich families taking a break from business

explanation: Spot on! Isolated villages struggle because bad roads and lack of basic infrastructure make it really hard to reach standard healthcare.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when patients want to use complementary or alternative therapies?

options.A: Forbidding patients from using any therapy not written in the doctor's orders
options.B: Personally performing massage and aromatherapy for every single patient
options.C: Ensuring safe use, providing education, and supporting patient preferences
options.D: Selling herbal supplements to patients to help fund the hospital ward

explanation: Well done! Nurses act as educators and safety advocates, helping patients safely blend alternative methods with their standard medical care.

question: Why is it tricky to study things like pain and fatigue in patients?

options.A: They only occur in male patients
options.B: They are abstract and hard to define uniformly
options.C: They never change over the course of an illness
options.D: They cannot be recorded on any medical chart

explanation: Exactly! Pain and fatigue look and feel different to every single person, which makes them harder to measure the same way every time.

question: A patient has a critically high potassium level. Which emergency medication combo helps push potassium out of the blood and back into the cells?

options.A: Aspirin and intravenous heparin
options.B: Furosemide and oral iron tablets
options.C: Normal saline and potassium chloride
options.D: Regular insulin and glucose

explanation: Brilliant! Insulin acts like a key to drive potassium safely back inside the cells, while glucose is given right along with it to keep the blood sugar stable.

question: What is the main reason doctors order blood screening tests for a patient exposed to unsafe injections?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of muscle mass in the limbs
options.B: To test for common food allergies and dietary sensitivities
options.C: To determine how quickly the patient's kidneys filter water
options.D: To check for the presence of blood-borne viral infections

explanation: Serological screening helps us catch antibodies or antigens for viruses like HIV or Hepatitis early, so the patient can get timely support.

question: What is the wonderful benefit of placing a newborn baby skin-to-skin on the mother's chest right after birth?

options.A: It helps maintain the baby's body temperature and promotes early breastfeeding
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the delivery of the remaining placenta

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact is magical! It keeps the baby warm, stabilizes their heart rate, and helps them find the breast easily. Nature at its finest!

question: What is the main sign that someone has a drug abuse problem?

options.A: Using vitamins for daily nutritional balance
options.B: Consuming natural herbs for mild headaches
options.C: Harmful or hazardous use despite negative consequences
options.D: Taking prescribed medications strictly as directed

explanation: Drug abuse means a person keeps using a substance even when it clearly harms their health, relationships, or daily life. You've got this!

question: Why is regular exercise and an active lifestyle good for a patient's bone health?

options.A: Lifestyle habits have no direct connection to skeletal strength
options.B: Weight-bearing exercise stimulates bone density and strengthens supporting muscles
options.C: Sedentary habits automatically increase vitamin D absorption in the skin
options.D: Exercise prevents all forms of genetic joint disease completely

explanation: Exactly right! Putting gentle physical stress on bones through movement tells the body to build stronger, denser bones.

question: Which specialized bone cell is responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteocyte
options.B: Osteoclast
options.C: Osteoblast
options.D: Chondrocyte

explanation: Remember: 'C' is for crush! Osteoclasts break down bone tissue to release minerals and help shape your bones.

question: Why do speech therapists and nurses sometimes add thickeners to drinks for dysphagia patients?

options.A: They slow down the flow rate to allow airway closure time
options.B: They prevent the liquid from tasting bitter to the patient
options.C: They provide extra calories and protein for wound healing
options.D: They stimulate the taste buds to increase appetite

explanation: Thin liquids rush down a weak throat way too fast before the epiglottis can close. Thickening the drink slows it down just enough for a safe swallow!

question: When measuring fluid from a drainage container, how should the nurse read the volume accurately?

options.A: By guessing the amount based on how full the bulb looks
options.B: By weighing the container on a bathroom scale while wet
options.C: By holding the container high up near the ceiling lights
options.D: At eye level with the liquid resting on a flat surface

explanation: Reading fluid levels at eye level on a flat surface prevents parallax errors and ensures the measurement recorded on the chart is correct. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why do nurses use the idea of a 'standard drink' instead of just counting glasses or bottles?

options.A: Serving sizes and alcohol strengths vary widely between different beverages
options.B: It makes tax calculations easier for local health authorities
options.C: Spirits contain no pure alcohol when mixed with water
options.D: Bottles of wine always contain exactly one standard serving

explanation: Not all drinks are poured equal! A big mug of stout packs way more punch than a small glass of wine. Using standard drinks helps patients track their real intake accurately.

question: A family member asks how to wash bed sheets stained with wound drainage. What should you tell them?

options.A: Wash the linens separately using hot water and standard detergent
options.B: Soak the linens in cold outdoor water before throwing them away
options.C: Wash the soiled sheets together with the family's weekly clothing
options.D: Hang the sheets in the sun without washing to kill the bacteria

explanation: Hot water and separate washing are key here! It breaks down the mess and stops germs from spreading to the rest of the household laundry.

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

options.A: It changes the recommended dosage for pediatric clients
options.B: It provides an easy entry route for environmental bacteria
options.C: It causes the liquid vaccine to freeze too quickly
options.D: It increases the expiration date printed on the label

explanation: Leaving a needle in the stopper breaks the closed seal of the vial, allowing airborne or contact germs to contaminate the remaining doses inside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Which common condition involves the weakening of bone due to rapid mineral loss from the spongy trabeculae?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoarthritis
options.D: Osteosarcoma

explanation: You've got this! Osteoporosis means 'porous bones.' It happens when bones lose minerals too quickly, making the tiny spongy struts thin out and break easily.

question: Which bone cell type is responsible for building new bone matrix?

options.A: Osteoclast
options.B: Osteogenic cell
options.C: Osteoblast
options.D: Osteocyte

explanation: Osteoblasts are the primary cells that build up and form new bone tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is it smart to involve traditional birth attendants (TBAs) in community safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To train them to recognize danger signs and refer women promptly
options.B: To grant them full authority to perform major surgeries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any modern medical clinics
options.D: To replace licensed nurses in major teaching hospitals

explanation: Many rural women trust TBAs. Training TBAs to spot trouble early means they can send mums to the hospital before it's too late.

question: How does overall energy balance affect a patient's body weight over time?

options.A: Consuming more calories than expended results in weight gain
options.B: BMR increases infinitely whenever extra food is eaten
options.C: Weight changes only occur if fluid balance is disturbed
options.D: Exercise alone determines weight without regard to food intake

explanation: Energy balance dictates that excess consumed calories are stored by the body, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h5)

question: What does the term 'orthostatic hypotension' mean?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.B: Swelling in the lower legs due to poor circulation
options.C: A spike in heart rate after eating heavy meals
options.D: High blood pressure caused by sleeping flat on the back

explanation: When blood vessels are slow to adjust to a new position, standing up too fast can cause a dizzy spell because of a sudden drop in pressure. Good to know for patient safety!

question: What is the main purpose of the feedback loop in the HPO (hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian) axis?

options.A: To regulate and coordinate hormone production between the brain and ovaries
options.B: To direct all excess hormones straight to the kidneys for filtration
options.C: To permanently shut down hormone release after puberty begins
options.D: To convert testosterone directly into adrenal adrenaline

explanation: Think of the feedback loop as a communication channel. The brain and ovaries talk back and forth to keep hormone levels balanced month after month.

question: When is surgical intervention required for a patient experiencing a haemorrhage?

options.A: Whenever external bleeding stops on its own
options.B: As the very first step before applying direct pressure
options.C: When internal bleeding cannot be stopped by non-surgical means
options.D: Only after the patient's blood pressure returns to normal

explanation: Surgery is necessary to physically find and repair damaged internal blood vessels or organs that external pressure cannot reach. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h7)

question: During triage at a disaster scene, which color tag goes to patients who can walk and only have minor cuts or scrapes?

options.A: Red
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Green

explanation: Think of 'Green' like a green light—these are the walking wounded who are stable and don't need emergency rushing to the theatre.

question: What is the main reason prolonged labour causes distress to the baby?

options.A: High levels of maternal thyroid hormones
options.B: Excessive production of amniotic fluid inside the sac
options.C: Reduced oxygen exchange across the compressed placenta
options.D: Rapid cooling of the baby's skin in the birth canal

explanation: Makes total sense! Strong, non-stop contractions squeeze the blood vessels in the placenta, meaning less oxygen gets through to the baby.

question: What is a must-do nursing action before giving any new medication to a patient?

options.A: Weighing the patient on a bed scale
options.B: Obtaining written consent from the family
options.C: Checking for known drug allergies
options.D: Drawing a baseline complete blood count

explanation: You nailed it! Always double-check allergy history first to avoid scary and dangerous reactions like anaphylaxis.

question: A patient arrives with active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). What kind of precautions should you set up right away?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Airborne precautions
options.D: Standard precautions only

explanation: Correct! TB travels easily through tiny air particles, so you need airborne precautions like a special room and an N95 mask.

question: Which statement best describes how research studies treat hypotheses?

options.A: The hypothesis is always proven wrong in clinical trials
options.B: Data either supports the hypothesis or fails to support it
options.C: A successful study proves the hypothesis is an absolute law
options.D: Hypotheses are proven true without needing statistical tests

explanation: Science is a journey! We don't claim absolute truth from one study; our data simply supports our guess or tells us to look closer.

question: What is the normal baseline range for a baby's heart rate during labor?

options.A: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 100 beats per minute
options.C: 170 to 200 beats per minute
options.D: 60 to 90 beats per minute

question: Which hormone tells the bone marrow to make more red blood cells during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Erythropoietin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Erythropoietin is like a special chemical messenger released by the kidneys to tell the bone marrow, 'Hey, we need more red blood cells for the baby!'

question: What is one of the main goals of maternal health services in a displacement camp?

options.A: Providing free formula milk to every newborn infant
options.B: Reducing maternal and neonatal mortality through skilled care
options.C: Eliminating the need for any antenatal checkups
options.D: Mandating home deliveries without professional assistance

explanation: Every mother deserves a safe delivery! Providing skilled midwives and emergency obstetric care saves mothers and newborns from avoidable complications in crisis zones.

question: What do you call a menu that repeats itself after a set time, like every two weeks?

options.A: Static menu
options.B: Single-use menu
options.C: A la carte menu
options.D: Cycle menu

question: How does a public health nurse help prevent abuse by starting a support group for young, first-time parents?

options.A: By forcing families to report their income to the government
options.B: By replacing the need for pediatric medical check-ups
options.C: By monitoring parents for illegal drug use in their homes
options.D: By building parenting skills and reducing social isolation

explanation: Connecting young parents with peers and teaching them parenting skills stops the loneliness and frustration that can lead to abuse.

question: What is the immediate next step after a school nurse identifies a health defect during a screening?

options.A: Providing a prompt referral for further clinical care
options.B: Keeping the finding secret from the parents
options.C: Prescribing specialized medicines immediately
options.D: Expelling the student from the school system

question: A community health nurse working in a rural Nigerian primary health care clinic is struggling to store vaccines properly due to frequent power outages. Which underlying systemic issue does this practical challenge highlight?

options.B: An overabundance of highly trained specialist surgeons in the village
options.C: Infrastructure deficits like erratic electricity affecting basic service delivery
options.D: A lack of willingness from mothers to immunize their babies

explanation: Logistical challenges such as power failures and supply chain gaps remain real hurdles in many Nigerian primary health centers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a rare but very serious complication unique to laparoscopy?

options.B: Mild tooth decay

options.D: Dry scalp scaling

question: Why do patients with metabolic acidosis often have abnormal potassium levels too?

options.A: Acidosis causes the pancreas to stop releasing insulin into the blood
options.B: The liver stores excess potassium whenever blood pH rises above normal
options.C: Potassium is directly converted into bicarbonate inside the glomerulus
options.D: Hydrogen and potassium ions share similar transport pathways in the kidneys

explanation: Think of hydrogen and potassium as rivals sharing the same doorway in the kidney. When there's too much acid (hydrogen), it affects how potassium is handled, often leading to a potassium imbalance.

question: What does the principle of informed choice mean for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Her family makes all healthcare decisions for her
options.B: She understands both the benefits and risks of home birth
options.C: She must choose a hospital regardless of her wishes
options.D: She can demand any medication she wants during labor

explanation: Informed choice requires that the mother is fully educated on what to expect, including potential dangers, before making her decision. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main health benefit of birth spacing for a mother?

options.A: Allows her body enough time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.B: Ensures all her children are the same gender
options.C: Guarantees she will never have morning sickness again
options.D: Eliminates the need for future antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Proper spacing prevents maternal depletion and gets the mother's body ready for a healthy future pregnancy.

question: Which of these is an immediate physical complication right after FGM?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Long-term post-traumatic stress
options.C: Infertility resulting from scarring
options.D: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
