question: What is Vitamin K's main role when it comes to blood clotting?

options.A: It dissolves dangerous blood clots in the veins
options.B: It helps the liver produce important clotting proteins
options.C: It constricts damaged blood vessels instantly
options.D: It stimulates the bone marrow to make platelets

explanation: Vitamin K is like a helper vitamin that your liver needs to build essential clotting factors. Without it, your blood cannot clot properly!

question: Which food nutrients are most important for keeping bones strong and posture upright?

options.A: Sodium and potassium
options.B: Vitamin C and iron
options.C: Protein and zinc
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are the ultimate dynamic duo for bone health! They build strong bones and help prevent weakness or spinal curving.

question: How do we tell an indirect obstetric cause of maternal death apart from a direct one?

options.A: It has no relation to the female reproductive system at all
options.B: It only happens during the third trimester of labor
options.C: It is exclusively caused by surgical errors
options.D: It is caused by a pre-existing medical condition worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Indirect causes are medical issues like heart disease or severe malaria that were already there, but got dangerously worse because of the physical changes of pregnancy.

question: Which of the following is an environmental factor that can lead to drug abuse?

options.A: Natural daily sleep cycle
options.B: Inherited eye color and height
options.C: Peer pressure and unemployment
options.D: Blood type A or positive O

explanation: Environmental factors are things happening around a person—like bad company (peer pressure) or joblessness—that push them toward drugs.

question: When is a scheduled caesarean section typically recommended for a pregnant woman living with HIV?

options.A: When the baby is presenting in a normal vertex position
options.B: When her viral load is high or unknown near delivery
options.C: When the mother prefers surgical delivery for convenience
options.D: When she has been taking her ART medications strictly

explanation: A planned caesarean delivery before labor starts helps lower the risk of infant exposure when viral suppression is not confirmed. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the key difference between active and passive range of motion?

options.A: Active is done by the patient alone, while passive is done with the nurse moving the joint
options.B: Active measures upper body joints, while passive measures lower body joints
options.C: Active is performed while standing, while passive is performed while lying down
options.D: Active uses a goniometer, while passive uses a measuring tape

explanation: Active movement relies on the patient's own muscle power, whereas passive movement relies on the nurse moving the relaxed limb. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the best way to help prevent slips and falls in the bathroom?

options.A: Removing grab bars to increase arm movement
options.B: Applying heavy floor wax to make tiles shine
options.C: Placing non-slip mats on wet tub and shower surfaces
options.D: Turning off bathroom lights to reduce glare

explanation: Non-slip mats give great traction on slippery tiles when soap and water are around. It's a quick win for patient safety!

question: A patient with a fever is breathing fast and sweating. What kind of fluid loss is happening here?

options.A: Measurable fluid output
options.B: Third-space fluid shift
options.C: Insensible fluid loss
options.D: Gastrointestinal loss

explanation: Exactly! It's called 'insensible' because we can't easily measure it with a jug or a catheter—it just silently evaporates away through breath and skin.

question: At what exact moment in your daily clinical routine should you sort and segregate hospital waste?

options.A: During the weekly facility audit
options.B: At the incinerator plant gate
options.C: At the exact point of generation
options.D: At the final municipal dumpsite

explanation: Always throw waste into the correct bin right where you use it! Sorting it immediately stops hazardous items from accidentally ending up in the general trash.

question: What is the main job of cold chain logistics in the food supply chain?

options.A: To keep transport vehicles cool for drivers on long trips
options.B: To freeze-dry grains for underground storage
options.C: To prevent the rapid spoilage of perishable items like milk and meat
options.D: To kill weed seeds in harvested crops before milling

explanation: Cold chain systems use refrigeration to keep perishable foods fresh and safe all the way from the farm to your plate.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure community members participate in a nutrition program?

options.A: Mobilizing community volunteers for distribution
options.B: Imposing strict rules without asking local opinions
options.C: Involving local leaders in the planning stages
options.D: Designing culturally appropriate interventions

explanation: Forcing programs on people without consulting them leads to poor participation and failure; community involvement is essential. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h5)

question: When public health experts calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio, what is the standard denominator used?

options.A: Per 10,000 total women
options.B: Per 100,000 live births
options.C: Per 1,000 live births
options.D: Per 1,000 pregnant women

explanation: Great to know for exams and clinical practice: maternal mortality ratio is always expressed per 100,000 live births. You're doing brilliantly!

question: Why does the body slow down digestion during pregnancy?

options.A: To allow more time for absorbing nutrients
options.B: To keep the maternal body temperature stable
options.C: To reduce pressure on the urinary bladder
options.D: To prevent the stomach from overstretching

explanation: Think of it as a helpful feature: slower digestion gives the body extra time to soak up all those important vitamins and nutrients for the growing baby!

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by your gut?

options.A: All known synthetic vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E, and K
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins like B and C
options.D: Only vitamin C and iron

explanation: Think of dietary fat as the vehicle that helps fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) travel across your intestinal wall into your bloodstream.

question: Why must everyone in a household get treated at the same time if one person has pinworms?

options.A: Untreated relatives will develop severe liver failure within forty-eight hours
options.B: Family members share identical genetic susceptibility to roundworm larvae
options.C: Single treatments are legally prohibited for treating minor household pests
options.D: Pinworms spread rapidly among family members through silent reinfection cycles

explanation: Pinworms spread so easily at home. If you only treat one person, everyone else passes the worms right back to them!

question: A patient has an open fracture with a small piece of bone sticking out of the skin. What is the correct initial nursing action?

options.A: Wash the exposed bone vigorously with strong antiseptic soap and water
options.B: Straighten the limb forcefully to hide the bone before taking an X-ray
options.C: Push the bone back inside the wound quickly and apply a tight tourniquet
options.D: Cover the wound loosely with a sterile dressing without pushing the bone in

explanation: Manipulating or pushing exposed bone back inside introduces deep infection, so the area must be covered loosely and left for the surgical team. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which liver enzyme is known to be more specific to liver cell injury?

options.A: AST
options.B: Amylase
options.C: ALT
options.D: Lipase

explanation: Spot on! Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is concentrated mostly inside liver cells, making it a reliable red flag when liver tissue is damaged.

question: During a home visit, your patient lets their adult child answer all your medical questions. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Refuse to discuss the care plan until the child leaves the room
options.B: Insist that the client make decisions completely on their own
options.C: Include the child in health education and care planning discussions
options.D: Report the family dynamic as a case of undue financial influence

explanation: Great choice! Respecting family structures means working together with the person they trust to speak for or help them.

question: Why must nurse-led dietary education consider a patient's cultural background and financial situation?

options.A: Hospital policies legally require patients to eat traditional hospital meals
options.B: Cultural foods are always lower in nutritional value than Western diets
options.C: Dietary advice only works if the patient can afford the foods and actually enjoys eating them
options.D: Financial status determines how fast human cells absorb dietary fiber

explanation: Patients are much more likely to stick to a meal plan if it respects their cultural food preferences and fits comfortably within their budget. Great job thinking practically!

question: What is the main focus of primordial prevention?

options.A: Rehabilitating patients after a stroke
options.B: Treating acute symptoms in a hospital ward
options.C: Broad social and environmental policies
options.D: Screening high-risk groups for hidden diseases

explanation: Primordial prevention tackles the root societal and environmental conditions that create health risks before they even start. You've got this!

question: What major nutrient do legumes like cowpeas (beans) and bambara groundnuts bring to our local pots?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Saturated animal fats
options.C: Plant-based protein
options.D: Simple sugars

explanation: Exactly right! Legumes and beans are fantastic, budget-friendly sources of protein, especially when meat isn't within reach.

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way to handle cultural diversity in learning?

options.A: Understanding that cultural backgrounds shape views on health and authority
options.B: Assuming every student learns and communicates in the exact same way
options.C: Recognizing diverse viewpoints to enrich classroom discussions
options.D: Creating a space where different communication styles are respected

explanation: Remember, we are all unique! Educators must embrace student diversity rather than expecting everyone to learn through a single mold.

question: How does popular media often misrepresent sexual intercourse to teenagers?

options.A: As casual, glamorous, and rarely involving negative consequences
options.B: As an activity that requires strict medical supervision
options.C: As something that only occurs among older adults
options.D: As an event that always results in immediate health complications

explanation: Media portrayals frequently glamorize sex while omitting discussions of contraception, consent, and infections, creating unrealistic expectations. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h7)

question: How does a risk assessment connect directly to a nursing care plan?

options.A: Nursing plans focus purely on hospital ward routines rather than community issues
options.B: Assessment findings identify the exact problems that the nursing plan aims to solve
options.C: Assessment data is only used for statistical research and never for nursing actions
options.D: Nursing plans are written first before any assessment is ever carried out

explanation: You assess first to discover the gaps (like dirty water or low immunization), and then you build your care plan to solve those exact problems!

question: What is the most common reason a patient with sickle cell anaemia is rushed to the emergency ward?

options.A: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis
options.C: Hypertensive emergency
options.D: Acute kidney failure

explanation: Spot on. When sickled cells block blood flow, tissues get starved of oxygen, triggering intense pain crises that bring patients straight to the hospital.

question: What is the primary nature of female physiological processes like menstruation and menopause?

options.A: Normal biological transitions
options.B: Temporary immune responses
options.C: Pathological endocrine disorders
options.D: Chronic degenerative diseases

explanation: Events like menstruation and menopause are healthy, expected life milestones rather than disease states. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is depending only on human brainpower and focus a risky strategy for patient safety?

options.A: Patients prefer automated machines to human nursing care
options.B: Nurses refuse to report mistakes when watching patients closely
options.C: Technology is always more expensive than hiring extra staff
options.D: Human beings experience fatigue and burnout, which inevitably leads to errors

explanation: Even the best nurses get tired during long shifts. That's why we need reliable systems, not just sheer willpower!

question: What is the main goal of gerontological nursing?

options.A: Emergency surgical interventions
options.B: Pediatric development milestones
options.C: Curative treatment for infectious diseases
options.D: Care of older adults and healthy aging

explanation: You've got this! Gerontological nursing is all about helping older adults live healthy, comfortable lives while managing long-term conditions. It's caring for the elderly with dignity.

question: What is the ultimate aim of dietary counselling?

options.A: Immediate cure of chronic viral infections
options.B: Total elimination of carbohydrates from the diet
options.C: Behavioral change regarding food habits
options.D: Reducing hospital kitchen operational costs

explanation: The main goal is to help patients change their actual eating behaviors for better long-term health outcomes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h2)

question: What is the main role of the mucociliary escalator in the nasal cavity?

options.A: To secrete specialized enzymes that dissolve food odors
options.B: To pump fresh oxygen directly into the pulmonary capillaries
options.C: To cool down overheated air before it enters the trachea
options.D: To transport trapped debris toward the throat for removal

explanation: Beating cilia move the sticky mucus layer backward so dust and bacteria are safely swallowed rather than entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h3)

question: What safety step must a nurse always take before transferring a patient into a wheelchair?

options.A: Secure the wheelchair and bed brakes
options.B: Give the patient a sedative drug
options.C: Raise the bed to the highest position
options.D: Remove all pillows from the room

explanation: Locking the wheels prevents the equipment from rolling away and causing a dangerous fall during the transfer. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which statement is the best example of supportive communication for a grieving family member?

options.A: 'At least your loved one is no longer suffering in pain.'
options.B: 'You have to stay strong for the rest of your young children.'
options.C: 'Don't worry, you will eventually find someone new to love.'
options.D: 'I am so sorry for your loss; I am here if you want to talk.'

explanation: You've got this! Acknowledging their pain directly and just being present is comforting, whereas cliché phrases can sound dismissive.

question: Where is the third ventricle located?

options.A: Within the central canal of the lumbar spinal cord
options.B: Directly beneath the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.C: Inside the core tissue of the cerebellum
options.D: Between the left and right halves of the thalamus

explanation: You're doing great! The third ventricle sits right in the middle, snuggled between the left and right sides of the thalamus.

question: Why are spore-forming bacteria so tough to clean out of the environment?

options.A: They can survive harsh environmental conditions and standard disinfectants for long periods
options.B: They require a human host to survive for more than a few seconds outdoors
options.C: They are completely invisible to all forms of standard laboratory microscope
options.D: They only multiply inside the bloodstream of healthy adult patients

explanation: Bacterial spores have tough little coats that help them shrug off normal cleaning methods and harsh weather, letting them hang around for ages.

question: A 16-year-old mother is getting ready for discharge after delivery. What is a top priority for her discharge education?

options.A: Information on filing for adult emancipation
options.B: Dietary guidelines for managing geriatric menopause
options.C: Instruction on how to return to competitive sports immediately
options.D: Contraception counseling to prevent rapid repeat pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Teenage mothers have a high chance of getting pregnant again too soon, so family planning guidance before discharge is vital.

question: Where is the body's center of gravity usually located when standing normally?

options.A: Inside the left ventricle
options.B: In the center of the pelvis
options.C: At the top of the skull
options.D: Directly between both feet

explanation: When standing straight, our center of balance or gravity is right around our pelvic area. Knowing this helps us understand how our bodies stay stable!

question: Why should a nurse worry if a patient stays on a clear fluid diet for days without extra nutrition?

options.A: The patient will lose all ability to swallow solid food forever.
options.B: The patient will quickly develop severe high blood pressure.
options.C: The patient's kidneys will immediately stop producing urine.
options.D: The patient is at high risk for malnutrition and delayed healing.

explanation: Without proteins and proper calories, wounds won't close and the body grows weak. Clear fluids are strictly short-term!

question: Why should a nurse explain neurological tests using simple, non-medical terms?

options.A: To shorten the overall duration of the hospital stay
options.B: To reduce patient anxiety and improve cooperation
options.C: To replace the need for a physical examination
options.D: To avoid documenting the assessment in the medical record

explanation: Clear and simple communication helps calm the patient so they can participate fully and accurately in the assessment. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient comes back to the clinic after losing 15 kg. What should you do as her nurse?

options.A: Instruct the client to continue using her current diaphragm device
options.B: Perform a repeat pelvic measurement for a new diaphragm size
options.C: Advise the client to stop using spermicide during intercourse
options.D: Recommend switching immediately to an oral contraceptive pill

explanation: Major weight changes shift body fat and pelvic tone, meaning she will likely need a new size for a snug, safe fit.

question: What is the main goal of community programs that prevent child abuse?

options.A: Removing all children from high-risk neighborhoods
options.B: Strengthening families and reducing stress before crises occur
options.C: Punishing parents who fail to attend community meetings
options.D: Replacing social welfare agencies with nurse-led clinics

explanation: Good prevention programs give parents the tools, coping skills, and support they need before things ever reach a crisis point.

question: Which core value means respecting a patient's right to make their own choices about their body and care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

explanation: Exactly! Autonomy is the ethical principle that protects a person's right to self-determination. It means patients call the shots on their own healthcare choices.

question: What does a mixed methods research study combine?

options.A: Hospital budgets and staffing rosters
options.B: Traditional habits and modern myths
options.C: Physician opinions and nursing guesses
options.D: Quantitative and qualitative approaches

explanation: You guessed it—mixed methods brings together both numerical data and narrative stories into one study!

question: Why would a bleeding disorder make a liver biopsy unsafe?

options.A: It can cause temporary muscle stiffness
options.B: It stops the kidneys from working properly
options.C: The liver has so many blood vessels, risking severe internal bleeding
options.D: It can cause a sudden skin infection

explanation: Correct! Because the liver is packed with blood vessels, a patient who cannot clot well is at high risk for dangerous internal bleeding.

question: What is the clinical term for when blood escapes from the blood vessels?

options.A: Hemostasis
options.B: Haemorrhage
options.C: Hypovolemia
options.D: Hemolysis

explanation: Haemorrhage is simply the medical word for bleeding. You've got this! Think of it as blood escaping its normal highway.

question: What is the origin of most cancer-causing mutations?

options.A: Passed down exclusively through maternal bloodlines
options.B: Inherited directly from parents in every single diagnosed case
options.C: Acquired over a lifetime from environmental and lifestyle factors
options.D: Caused entirely by sudden bacterial infections in childhood

explanation: Most cancers arise from acquired mutations that build up over time due to exposure to external agents like tobacco, radiation, and unhealthy diets. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which type of budget takes care of daily running costs like medical supplies and generator fuel?

options.A: Emergency surplus budget
options.B: Capital budget
options.C: Operational budget
options.D: Personal investment budget

explanation: The operational budget keeps the lights on and the supplies stocked for everyday patient care.

question: Why should a nurse view reproductive choices as part of a broader life plan?

options.A: Because personal goals, health, and finances deeply affect family size choices
options.B: Because government policies require strict tracking of household income
options.C: So that medical treatments can be delayed until retirement age
options.D: To ensure the nurse can dictate the exact number of children a client has

explanation: Reproductive decisions do not happen in a vacuum; they are shaped by an individual's financial situation, overall health status, and future life aspirations. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h1)

question: How often should emergency crash carts and equipment usually be checked?

options.A: Once every month
options.B: Only after a code blue occurs
options.C: At the start of every shift
options.D: During annual hospital accreditation

explanation: Correct! Checking the crash cart every shift ensures everything is present, unexpired, and working before an emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is a normal, harmless feeling a patient might report right after getting an IV contrast injection?

options.A: Severe sharp pain in the chest
options.B: Sudden numbness in both lower legs
options.C: A warm flushing feeling and metallic taste
options.D: An intense urge to vomit continuously

explanation: It's totally normal for patients to feel a sudden warm rush and taste metal in their mouth. Warn your patients beforehand so they don't panic!

question: How do traditional beliefs often mischaracterize women who have not undergone FGM?

options.A: As being unable to bear healthy children
options.B: As being hypersexual and prone to promiscuity
options.C: As lacking basic community survival skills
options.D: As suffering from chronic physical weakness

explanation: Correct! Cultural myths wrongly claim that unoperated women cannot control their sexual urges.

question: What is the truest way to know if a continuing education training program was actually successful?

options.A: Checking how many participants filled out the seminar evaluation form
options.B: Verifying that all attendees stayed awake throughout the presentation
options.C: Observing if nurses apply what they learned to improve patient bedside care
options.D: Counting how many hours the lecture room lights remained switched on

explanation: Paper evaluations are nice, but real success shows up at the bedside when patients receive better, safer care because of what you learned!

question: Which nutrient-rich foods are very often forbidden to pregnant women in many traditional settings?

options.A: Cassava flakes
options.B: Hard white yam
options.C: Refined table salt
options.D: Eggs and meat

explanation: Protein-packed items like eggs, snails, and meat are frequent targets of pregnancy food taboos due to old cultural myths.

question: A patient with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways is most likely to be prescribed which type of inhalable medication?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Vasopressors
options.D: Mucolytics

question: Why is working together across different agencies so vital during a major public health emergency?

options.A: External security forces take complete legal ownership of medical patient charts
options.B: Government regulations mandate that all agencies merge into a single permanent ministry
options.C: No single agency has enough resources or personnel to handle a major disaster alone
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to perform clinical triage duties in hospitals

explanation: Disasters are too big for just one group. By combining health workers, security, and transport agencies, everyone pitches in to save lives.

question: What is the primary role of the pyramidal motor tracts?

options.A: Transmitting pain signals from the feet
options.B: Controlling fine, skilled voluntary movements
options.C: Maintaining unconscious balance and posture
options.D: Regulating involuntary heart muscle contractions

explanation: Spot on! Pyramidal tracts carry direct messages from the cortex for those precise, delicate movements we rely on.

question: How can hospital management best help nurses overcome barriers to using research?

options.A: Requiring every nurse to publish a textbook before promotion
options.B: Providing access to journal databases and encouraging ward journal clubs
options.C: Punishing nurses who ask questions about traditional ward routines
options.D: Banning all clinical discussions during the morning handover shift

explanation: Brilliant! Creating an encouraging learning environment with easy resource access makes research feel friendly and doable for the whole team.

question: Why shouldn't you force a survivor to tell every single detail of their assault right away?

options.A: Forced retelling can trigger severe anxiety and re-traumatize the patient
options.B: Police investigations are always hindered by early patient statements
options.C: Medical records do not need any details about the assault
options.D: Physical examination results become invalid if the patient speaks

explanation: Let survivors take their time. Pressing them to talk too soon can overwhelm them and bring back the trauma.

question: Why do physical signs of puberty usually show up long after the internal hormonal changes have already started?

options.A: Because the skin blocks hormones from reaching the rest of the body early on
options.B: Because bones refuse to lengthen until a person turns twelve years old
options.C: Because internal chemical signals must build up and stimulate target organs over time
options.D: Because children eat too many processed foods before growing up

explanation: Well done! Hormones start working quietly behind the scenes in the brain way before you can actually see any physical changes on the outside.

question: Why is keeping our core body temperature within a steady, normal range so important?

options.A: To keep the skeletal muscles from contracting too quickly
options.B: To prevent the bones from becoming brittle over time
options.C: To support normal metabolic processes and cellular function
options.D: To ensure the digestive system absorbs enough water

explanation: Spot on! Our body's chemical reactions and tiny cellular engines need a stable temperature to run smoothly without breaking down.

question: How does sharing health data across different sectors help the system?

options.A: It allows private hospitals to control public health budgets
options.B: It stops patients from visiting primary health centers
options.C: It ensures that patients never have to pay medical bills
options.D: It helps leaders forecast outbreaks and allocate staff efficiently

explanation: When health data is pooled together, leaders can spot disease outbreaks early and place nurses and staff where they are needed most.

question: How does keeping a young girl in school directly help prevent early marriage?

options.A: It empowers her with knowledge, raises her aspirations, and delays marriage age.
options.B: It exempts her from all future household and domestic duties.
options.C: It legally emancipates her from her parents on her twelfth birthday.
options.D: It automatically grants her family a monthly government stipend.
